THE PROBLEMKnow what needs
a closer look.

Safety managers and disaster responders need to understand hazards before deciding where to inspect or enter. Zipbul helps them review what was observed, where it is and why it matters in an explorable 3D scene.

Why spatial exploration matters: NIST describes drone imagery and indoor mapping as tools for locating people and potential hazards during disaster response. This motivates Zipbul's approach to spatial review. NIST, 2025 ↗

Three modules. One exploration vision.

Control / Capture / Review

01ZipControl

Uses drone camera images to plan and select actions, then operates the Android control app's joysticks without a drone SDK. Actual drone flight control was demonstrated.

02ZipScan

Captures mesh, video, camera poses and depth with iPhone LiDAR. Geometric projection turns recorded imagery into a textured GLB while preserving the captured mesh.

03ZipBul

Imports GLB and source video, proposes inspection candidates and links them to visual evidence. Users explore the scene, verify locations and review relationships between findings.

Built with OpenAI & Codex
Project brief / October 2026

Intelligence, grounded in action.

OpenAI models handle visual interpretation and decisions. Geometry connects observations to the scene, and people can inspect the evidence behind each candidate.

OpenAI in the product

Astra plans. Luna acts.

GPT-6 Astra turns camera observations and a mission into a subgoal. GPT-6 Luna, through the Decisions API, repeatedly selects an allowed action or requests replanning from current and previous camera crops.

GPT-6 AstraVisual reasoning + subgoal
GPT-6 LunaImage-based action choice
Luna's accepted action maps to Android joystick input.

In ZipBul, Astra identifies inspection candidates in sampled video frames. Camera pose, depth and mesh intersections provide location proposals.

Measured API latency

Faster median
action selection.

Astra baseline3.31 s
Luna Decisions0.56 s

20 calls per model; 740 × 540 image and goal. Astra: function arguments. Luna: enum choice.

Codex in development

Two developers.
Three modules.

We split hardware integration and scanning from the main analysis app, running Codex agents in parallel within one monorepo. Shared data contracts kept the modules aligned under hackathon time constraints.

With Astra in Codex, we implemented Android input control, camera-and-depth texture projection, and video-to-3D mapping. Codex was our sole AI coding tool; all AI models and services were from OpenAI.

What we demonstrated

01 / Actual flight

Drone flight control through the Android app was demonstrated. The linked video shows the airborne drone and the running ZipControl interface.

02 / Real field data

Scanned Centerfield's 18th and ground floors. One 10-minute ground-floor video yielded 16 inspection candidates from 41 sampled frames.

03 / Reviewable results

Verified source-video access, saved manual location links, relationship graphs, and walkthrough movement and collisions. Candidates remain subject to human review.

Vision / Disaster response and industrial safety

Understand hard-to-reach places before people enter.

Connect remote exploration, spatial capture and evidence-based hazard analysis to support inspection priorities in industrial facilities and disaster sites. Extend today's human-collected scans to drone and robot capture under human supervision.
